subject: Procurement timetable & legal lanes — proposed sync play for Cardinal Health
messages:
From: Marta Delgado <marta.delgado@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: John Park <john.park@cardinalhealth.com>, procurement@cardinalhealth.com
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement timetable & legal lanes — Cardinal next steps

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo earlier this week. Legal and procurement asked me to put together a short timeline that captures the dependencies across MSA, DPA and the order form so we can identify parallel workstreams. Attaching a compact RFP summary and the questions procurement flagged.

High level ask: can Redwood provide a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) that shows:
- legal review window for MSA/DPA (names/owners)
- procurement approval milestone and PO timing
- any compliance artifacts we need (SOC2, data retention, encryption specifics)
- target signature window by end of July if we can fast-track reviews

We want to avoid full sequential gating — ideally legal reviews run in parallel with procurement pricing approval. We're open to a short carve-out for order form price lock until legal redlines are settled.

Can you turn around a draft MAP and a suggested sprint timetable by Monday? John (cc) will be the legal contact for redlines.

Thanks,
Marta

--
Marta Delgado
Sr. Procurement Manager, Cardinal Health
attachments: Cardinal_MA_Platform_RFP.pdf (PDF, 420KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marta Delgado <marta.delgado@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, John Park <john.park@cardinalhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement timetable & legal lanes — Cardinal next steps

Marta — thanks for the clear ask and the RFP. We're on it. Quick plan from my side:

1) Draft a concise MAP (one slide + spreadsheet) that splits workstreams into: commercial (order form & pricing), legal (MSA + DPA redlines), security & compliance (evidence handoff).
2) Propose a "parallel review" timeline so procurement pricing approval and legal redlines overlap by ~7–10 business days.
3) Include a contingency: an interim price lock on the order form that binds pricing but allows the MSA/DPA language to finish.

I'll attach a first-pass MAP and a sprint timetable in this thread (redwood_syncplay_draft_v1.xlsx). Lauren will own procurement coordination and Aditya will coordinate the SOC2/evidence handoff. John — any constraints from legal we should bake into the timeline (e.g., minimum review cycles, security sign-off before signature)?

Deliverable ETA: Monday 2026-06-29 EOD PST. If you prefer, we can run a 30-min alignment call after you review.

Karthik
--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_syncplay_draft_v1.xlsx (Excel, 75KB)

From: John Park <john.park@cardinalhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marta Delgado <marta.delgado@cardinalhealth.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement timetable & legal lanes — Cardinal next steps

Karthik / team —

Thanks for the draft. A few legal constraints to call out so the MAP reflects reality:
- We can run MSA and DPA redlines in parallel, but we need a single source-of-truth repo for redline comments (DocuSign/SharePoint link preferred).
- Security attestation (SOC2) must be received and validated before the DPA is signed — we can accept the attestation PDF and a short runbook of controls (we have the SOC2 doc attached to this email).
- For faster approval, we prefer an interim order form that captures term length, seat counts, and a price commitment clause with a 30-day conditional signature hold while legal completes final language.
- Please surface any non-negotiable Redwood clauses up front (data residency, subprocessor list).

If we can keep the commercial team engaged and not wait for final legal sign-off, procurement can issue the PO with a conditional acceptance. That will get your pilots funded faster.

John

--
John Park
Senior Counsel, Cardinal Health
attachments: SOC2_Attestation_2025.pdf (PDF, 210KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Marta Delgado <marta.delgado@cardinalhealth.com>, John Park <john.park@cardinalhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement timetable & legal lanes — Cardinal next steps

Hi Marta / John — looping back with an updated plan after we ingested your notes. Key items below (I've attached the updated MAP spreadsheet with milestones):

- Sprint rundown (week numbers):
  * Week 1 (Jul 5–9): Legal kickoff (MSA/DPA initial redlines), procurement to confirm budget owner and PO template.
  * Week 2 (Jul 12–16): Parallel redline iteration (legal) + SOC2 evidence validation (security).
  * Week 3 (Jul 19–23): Final commercial term review and price lock exercised (order form interim).
  * Week 4 (Jul 26–30): Target signature window — procurement issues conditional PO the week of Jul 26; final sign-off once legal completes DPA.

- Owner matrix:
  Redwood commercial: Lauren (procurement liaison), Karthik (deal owner)
  Redwood security: Aditya (evidence handoff)
  Cardinal procurement: Marta (PO owner)
  Cardinal legal: John (redlines)

- Immediate asks for Cardinal to unblock Week 1:
  1) Confirm PO approver name & PO template (procurement@cardinalhealth.com).
  2) Share any non-negotiable clauses (data residency or required subprocessor approvals).
  3) Confirm a preferred doc repo for redlines (we propose SharePoint; DocuSign for final execution).

Attachments: redwood_syncplay_draft_v1.xlsx (updated), plus a short checklist in the sheet called "Week0-Prep".

If that aligns, we'll set a 30-min kickoff for Tue Jul 6 to run the dependencies and owners.

Thanks — Lauren
--
Lauren Bishop
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
